text: Where the 24 known letters leave an unknown alphabet undecided, a likely word placed somewhere else adds more letters to check. If K4 is such a code, the right words should fit it more often than they fit scrambled copies.
Sixty words at every place they can go, each placement decided exactly, in the ten settings still open: one alphabet at key lengths 23 and 26, two alphabets at eight lengths.
K4 fits no more often than its copies: above all ten in one setting, as the copies themselves manage 0 to 3 times. F12.6 closed.
